articles.title: Professor Layton Developer Level-5 Scrambles to Reupload Trailers as AI Backlash Intensifies
articles.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
articles.content:
In the wake of fierce online backlash, Professor Layton developer Level-5 has released a new statement apologizing for the mistrust caused by generative AI use in its recent showcase for upcoming titles, insisting some examples spotted by fans were simply human error.
Not only that, but the studio has insisted that some mistakes flagged as AI errors by eagle-eyed commenters on social media were actually human mistakes. The Japanese studio has now vowed to clean up these offending portions.
For those who missed it, Level-5 released its “VISION 2026 II: Dreams” presentation on YouTube on September 10. Narrated by a cartoon version of CEO Akihiro Hino, the showcase walked viewers through the studio’s upcoming releases, including Yokai Watch 2: Haunted Domain, Decapolice, and a first look at Professor Layton and the New World of Steam.
However, shortly after the video dropped, social media was flooded with comments and reaction videos. Commenters scrutinized backgrounds and art, noting inconsistencies and elements suggestive of generative AI use, with many slamming Level-5 for perceived “AI slop.” Comparisons between the September 9 Nintendo Direct Yokai Watch 2 trailer and the VISION 2026 trailer for the same game released just a day later also had fans pointing out AI-like errors. The Nintendo Direct trailer for Professor Layton and the Curious Village (a Switch remake of the Nintendo DS original), also had internet sleuths finding elements that appeared to be AI upscales of original backgrounds.
Oh no Level-5 is DEFINATELY using Gen AI to "update" Professor Layton. Especially when you compare the original backgrounds to the new. So many weird details and inconsistencies were added. https://t.co/AjVNfgetkk pic.twitter.com/0tRQ9vKn03
— AmericanYoshi (@AmericanYoshi) September 10, 2026
This backlash prompted CEO Hino to make a statement on X, admitting that the developer had experimented with using AI processing techniques for the VISION 2026 II showcase out of a “desire to make the presentation flashy." After apologizing for the offense that this caused, Hino insisted that key elements of Level-5's games (such as story, character designs and settings) were created by people and that AI tools were used to speed up the process of digitizing artists’ creations. “Please be reassured that there is no simplistic, AI-generated data in our released games,” Hino commented, before noting that the company’s use of AI tools to make processes more efficient was giving its developers more time to be creative, and that they are currently in a trail-and-error process of shortening the 5-year development cycle for major titles down to two years.
Hino’s statement went down like a lead balloon, however. The CEO’s comments about “using AI in various ways” to enhance the visual appearance of the showcase drew particular ire, with many Japanese users seeing this as a lazy ‘style over substance’ approach. “Isn’t the point of a trailer to express creativity, not flashiness?” one person said.
Many commenters in both Japanese and English also pointed out the ethical issues with how generative AI has been trained on copyrighted works of artists, and how Level-5’s attitude towards gen AI creates distrust among fans. “I think human spirit is more important than the speed of game releases, so wouldn’t it be better to not use AI, even if it takes five years? Even if just one asset is AI-generated, people will never stop worrying about whether a song, image or line of dialogue is AI or human-made. Isn’t maintaining trust the most important thing?” another commenter responded in Japanese. As a side note, Level-5’s concept image for its TGS booth also got flagged as a suspected AI image, prompting further angry comments.
In its latest statement issued on September 17, Level-5 said: “We deeply apologize for the distrust in our production process that our inexperienced use of AI and simple human errors have caused. Please note that AI has not been used directly in the contents of the games themselves. Moving forward, we will pay even greater attention to the accuracy and quality of the work we produce.”
Level-5 also said that it will clean up “errors caused by AI use, as well as human mistakes that look like AI errors,” and upload corrected versions of the trailers to coincide with Tokyo Game Show, which opens to the public this weekend. At the time of writing, Level-5 has uploaded TGS versions of trailers for Decapolice and Holy Horror Mansion to its official YouTube channel.
In its September 17 statement, Level-5 published a side-by-side of Yokai Watch 2’s promotional illustration before and after mistakes had been edited out. Addressing comments made by users regarding the telephone lines looking “unnatural,” the company stated that its artist had used a real photo of telephone lines they had taken themselves as a reference, and intentionally simplified the lines to fit the background, which resulted in this “being misconstrued as AI.” “These telephone lines were actually hand-drawn by our in-house designer, however, to prevent any further misunderstandings, we have corrected them so that they look more natural,” Level-5 said.
But what about other details flagged by commenters as possible signs of gen AI usage? Level-5 said that, “Similarly, other issues that people pointed out, such as with the vending machine and guttering, were also the result of human error in omitting these details. The brake levers on the bicycle were not drawn in past Yokai Watch 2 games. However, we feel they should have been drawn for this latest game, considering the higher level of detail.”
⁉️ Dans le nouveau trailer de Yo-kai Watch 2 : Haunted Domain, Nathan a… changé de visage ?! 😭#YOKAIWATCH
Hier (gauche) / Aujourd’hui (droite) pic.twitter.com/Vr3rzwNPA7
Many commenters also picked up on how Kenta/Nathan’s face looks different in the Level-5’s VISION 2026 II showcase and the Nintendo Direct that was released on the previous day. In response, Level-5 said, “We did not make any alterations or corrections using AI.” It said it was unable to correct Nathan’s low-poly appearance in time for Nintendo Direct’s submission deadline but had updated the model by the time of its own showcase, which explains why Nathan looks different in trailers that were made public just one day apart. Level-5 also stated that “no AI was used in Professor Layton and the New World of Steam,” however it did not comment on whether or not AI was used for the Curious Village remake.
Level-5 wrapped up its statement by apologizing again for the distrust caused by its “inexperienced use of AI and human error," promising to take more care in the future to avoid such mistakes. “From now on, we will limit our AI usage to enhancing efficiency, and will avoid directly using it in videos released directly to our fans.”
This statement also did not go down well. “I don’t think they understand WHY using AI is bad. We weren’t mad at the little errors that AI produced, we just used those errors to determine if it was AI or not, because using AI at all is bad. Now they are going to continue using AI but they are going to hide it better,” one commenter responded.
It's not about reducing the use of AI, but about eliminating it entirely. pic.twitter.com/ziJuMrxBsm
— Turo (@Any_Turo) September 16, 2026
Many Japanese comments also criticized the Level-5 statement for blaming human error. “You promised not to use gen AI going forward, but aren’t you just shifting the blame onto the staff?” replied one commenter. “I think the main reason for all this criticism is President Hino’s stance of repeatedly promoting generative AI usage without confronting its fundamental issues (such as unauthorized use of data and environmental pollution).”
Level-5 has been experimenting with gen AI tools to speed up game development and improve efficiency for at least the last three years. Back in December 2023, the studio released an extensive presentation on its use of AI tools to a Japanese government study group (source: Automaton/ITMedia). In short, it has been using Stable Diffusion to generate layout ideas for promotions, and to create 3D versions of the original 2D models from older games, like its Yokai Watch series. However, the company pointed out then that these generative AI outputs were just used as guidelines for its human artists, who produced the final output. In the same presentation, it described combining parts of AI-generated images with creations by its artists to make the in-game backgrounds (including stadium crowds and buildings) for soccer RPG Inazuma Eleven: Victory Road.
However, it remains to be seen how much the studio’s attitude towards AI usage costs it in terms of players’ trust in the company.

Level-5 has issued a formal apology and pledged to revise promotional materials after fans identified suspected generative AI artifacts in recent trailers for upcoming titles like Professor Layton.

### Key Points
- Level-5 released the "VISION 2026 II: Dreams" showcase on September 10, featuring titles such as *Decapolice* and *Professor Layton and the New World of Steam*.
- Social media users identified visual inconsistencies in trailers, prompting accusations of "AI slop" and concerns regarding the use of generative tools in game development.
- CEO Akihiro Hino admitted to using AI for "flashy" presentation effects but insisted that no AI-generated data is present within the actual game software.
- The studio attributed several flagged errors to human mistakes, such as simplified hand-drawn background elements, and promised to release corrected trailer versions.
- Level-5 stated it will limit future AI usage to internal efficiency tasks and avoid using it in public-facing promotional videos to restore fan trust.

### Why it Matters
The backlash highlights a growing tension between game developers seeking to accelerate production cycles and a player base increasingly wary of generative AI's ethical and creative implications. By failing to fully address concerns regarding the technology's role in their workflow, Level-5 risks long-term damage to its brand reputation and consumer loyalty.

articles.title: Align Technology Sees Invisalign Growth Runway Despite Consumer Headwinds
articles.author: MarketBeat
articles.content:
Align Technology NASDAQ: ALGN sees continued growth potential for Invisalign clear aligners in the United States and internationally despite a challenging consumer environment, Chief Financial Officer John Morici said during a Baird investor conference.
Morici said inflation and patient reluctance to begin treatment have weighed on the orthodontics market over roughly the past 18 months. Those pressures can influence how orthodontists and general practitioners invest in their practices and whether patients move forward with treatment.
Still, he said the company sees substantial room to replace traditional wires-and-brackets treatments with clear aligners. Morici said approximately 75% of combined teen and adult orthodontic cases in North America are still performed using wires and brackets.
“We have a huge opportunity to grow in U.S., just like the rest of the world, to get clear aligners, to have Invisalign,” Morici said.
Product and Financing Efforts Target Conversion
Morici said Align is seeking to help doctors compete with the upfront economics of traditional orthodontic treatment by offering products with fewer included refinements. Those offerings can lower initial costs for practices compared with more comprehensive products, while giving doctors the option to pay for refinements later if needed.
The company is also emphasizing consumer financing options, which Morici described as increasingly important in converting potential patients. Align has worked with Healthcare Finance Direct and other lenders, he said, while also seeing financing become a larger consideration in Europe and other international markets.
In addition to financing, Morici said visualization tools that show prospective patients what their teeth may look like after treatment can support conversion at orthodontic and general-practice offices.
Align’s no-AA, or no-refinement, product initially launched with certain dental service organizations, or DSOs, in the U.S. and is being introduced to retail doctors. Morici said adoption has been favorable, although doctors must plan cases carefully when using products designed for limited or no refinements.
He said the strategy is intended to expand utilization by helping doctors choose Invisalign in situations where they might otherwise use wires and brackets because of a lower lab bill. While the company may collect less cash upfront on some cases, Morici said doctors using the products have tended to perform more Invisalign cases.
  - Align said no-refinement products can support gross-margin improvement by reducing the number of refinements in the product mix.
- The company is also offering touch-up and lower-stage products intended to meet different clinical and pricing needs.
- Morici said Align’s focus is primarily on converting wires-and-brackets cases rather than simply taking share from other clear-aligner providers.
International Growth and New Product Rollouts
Morici said international markets remain underpenetrated and have responded well to newer products, including Invisalign Personalization Experience, or IPE, and touch-up offerings. Align has expanded certain products into Europe and Asia-Pacific, including DSP in Asia during the second half of the year, he said.
He noted that 55% of Align’s business is outside North America and said that business has been growing at double-digit rates. India, Southeast Asia and Brazil have shown strong growth following investments in sales and marketing resources, according to Morici.
Within North America, he said DSOs account for about one-third of the company’s regional business and have also been growing at double-digit rates. The company’s key area of focus is North American retail business, which Morici characterized as roughly 30% of Align’s overall operations.
When discussing the company’s outlook, Morici said Align bases its guidance on recent business trends, current market conditions and product introductions rather than solely on year-over-year comparisons. He said Align’s first-half case volume rose about 7% on average, while its second-half guidance implied approximately 5% to 6% year-over-year volume growth.
China Volume-Based Procurement Could Expand Access
Morici also addressed China’s orthodontic volume-based procurement, or VBP, process. Align currently operates predominantly in China’s private market, but Morici said the company expects the effects of VBP on public providers to extend to private pricing over time.
He said about 90% of orthodontic cases in China are performed with wires and brackets, while clear aligners remain a relatively small part of the market. Align expects its portfolio, ranging from comprehensive to more moderate and lower-stage cases, to allow it to compete in the VBP environment.
While pricing pressure could emerge, Morici said Align could gain volume by reaching doctors who previously did not use its products. He also pointed to the company’s manufacturing and treatment-planning operations in China as potential cost offsets.
The VBP process could create opportunities for Align to participate in public hospitals where it has had less exposure, he said. The company would evaluate tenders based on whether pricing, incremental revenue and costs make economic sense.
Margin Framework and Research Spending
Morici said Align is pursuing productivity initiatives alongside volume growth, including shifting some manufacturing closer to regional markets to reduce freight costs and delivery times. He also cited a planned India facility focused on serving the Indian market, which he said could improve cycle times while reducing customs and duty costs.
He reiterated the company’s focus on structural profitability improvements, including product mix and operational programs. Morici said Align has discussed about 100 basis points of operating-margin improvement for the current year and at least 100 basis points for the following year.
On research and development, Morici said spending should gain leverage as products move from research into development and commercialization. He said investments in direct fabrication, resin technology and the iTero Lumina platform have increasingly shifted toward development, though the company intends to continue investing in technology and innovation.
About Align Technology (NASDAQ:ALGN)
Align Technology, Inc NASDAQ: ALGN is a global medical device company that designs, manufactures and markets products used in orthodontics and digital dentistry. Its best-known product is the Invisalign system, a series of clear, removable aligners intended to gradually straighten teeth and address certain orthodontic conditions under the supervision of dental professionals.
The company also develops digital dentistry technologies, including iTero intraoral scanners and related software, which create digital impressions and support orthodontic, restorative and implant treatment planning.

Align Technology CFO John Morici highlighted growth strategies for Invisalign, focusing on converting traditional wire-and-bracket patients to clear aligners despite ongoing economic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

### Key Points
- Align Technology aims to capture the 75% of North American orthodontic cases currently treated with traditional wires and brackets.
- The company is introducing lower-cost, no-refinement products to help dental practices compete more effectively on price.
- International markets, particularly in India, Southeast Asia, and Brazil, are currently driving double-digit growth for the company.
- Align is expanding consumer financing options through partnerships to help patients manage treatment costs amid a challenging economic environment.
- Management expects 100 basis points of operating-margin improvement annually through productivity initiatives and localized manufacturing.

### Why it Matters
Align’s strategy to prioritize market conversion over traditional orthodontics is critical for sustaining long-term growth in a saturated dental sector. By lowering entry costs and expanding financing, the company aims to maintain its competitive edge against traditional methods while navigating global economic volatility.
